text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has demanded a rapid reponse to the question of which sports arenas will be built if Stockholm is chosen to host the 2004 Olympic Games. The decision must be made by October 23 at the latest.
- Industry minister Anders Sundstrom says Sweden will need to build a new gas-fired power station to enable the country to phase out nuclear power as planned.

- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) is losing passengers on important domestic lines such as Stockholm - Gothenburg to the Swedish railways' X2000 high-speed trains. The X2000 began to take market share last year and the trend looks like continuing.
- Top bosses at engineering group ABB have been paid bonuses in tax havens in the West Indies. CEO Percy Barnevik will have to declare a 500,000 crown bonus paid in 1993 as taxable income.

- Gas producer AGA is moving its production closer to the customer. The company is to inaugurate a new oxygen production plant on site at Avesta Sheffield's Swedish steel mill later on Thursday, the first plant of its type in Sweden.
- A protracted fall in Swedish debt yields is set to continue, particularly at the long end of the yield curve where many investors are buying government bonds "like mad".

- Telecoms group Ericsson aims to provide faster Internet link-ups through more efficient use of the existing phone network. The system is ready for use and Ericsson expects the market to be worth several billion crowns.

- The Swedish Finance Inspectorate is to probe all of the ramifications of the Morgan Grenfell affair in Sweden. The investment banking arms of S-E-Banken, Nordbanken and Carnegie will all have to account for their dealings with Morgan Grenfell's share funds.
